Fairbairn has established himself as one of the busiest and most accurate kickers in the league, which is an excellent combination for fantasy purposes. He remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ka'imi Fairbairn has connected on all seven of his field-goal attempts over Houston's past two games after going just 4-for-5 through Week 3. He's among the most reliable kickers in the league and can be started with confidence in Week 6 despite a tricky matchup against the Jaguars, who have allowed just seven made field goals and 14.0 points per game through five games. Fairbairn is 55-for-60 on field-goal attempts in 20 regular-season appearances since the start of last season, including a perfect 42-for-42 from inside 50 yards.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season for the Texans and remains a high-end starting fantasy kicker for Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense is trending in the wrong direction. The Giants allowed just 18.3 points per game through Week 3 but have surrendered 28.3 points per game across their last three, including 34 to the Saints in Week 6. Meanwhile, the Texans have won two consecutive games after starting 0-4, and Fairbairn has made all nine of his field-goal attempts over the past three weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rome Odunze will seek to do more as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Odunze was unable to capitalize on the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, as he finished the game with two catches for 52 yards. The third-year receiver still figures to be a top target for Caleb Williams moving forward, especially in closer matchups where a consistent option is needed. Odunze will face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points to WRs (55.2) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rome Odunze will look to improve on modest production as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Odunze reeled in three of six targets for 44 yards against the Eagles in Week 3, adding to his already disappointing start to the season. The third-year wide receiver has been consistent, recording three or fewer catches for 52 or fewer yards in each of Chicago's first three games. Odunze will face a Jets squad that has allowed the fourth-fewest receiving yards (337) to WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rome Odunze will look to build off a big performance as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Odunze was on fire in Week 4 against the Jets with Tyson Bagent under center, bringing in six of seven targets for 94 yards. The starting wide receiver has now posted a 14-233-0 receiving line on the year, which leaves plenty of room to grow. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 31.8 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rome Odunze remains a top option in Chicago's passing game ahead of Week 6 at Atlanta. Odunze brought in just three of his nine targets for 40 yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, but he still ranked second in receiving yards. The volatility of the Bears' quarterback position has affected Odunze's production so far this season, so the return of Caleb Williams would likely be favorable. Either way, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rome Odunze will look to do more as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Odunze brought in just three of four targets for 39 yards in Week 6, which was a bit of a bummer, with Caleb Williams throwing for 305 yards. The third-year pass catcher has been held in check in more games than not this season, catching 20 of 33 targets for 312 yards with zero touchdowns. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, and those mistakes could catch up against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite Brock Bowers missing the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kirk Cousins went down swinging in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, setting season highs with 52 pass attempts and 365 yards while throwing multiple TDs for a fourth straight game to begin the season. While rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza waits in the wings, Cousins' 11 touchdowns are tied for the league lead, and he sits just outside the top 10 in passing yards and completion rate, which should give him plenty of job security. The veteran quarterback will try to keep rolling in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kirk Cousins' production is declining, potentially reducing his time as the Raiders' starting quarterback. After throwing for nine touchdowns during the team's 3-0 start to the season, the veteran has a 3:1 TD:INT over the last two contests, both losses. During a lopsided Week 5 loss to the Patriots, Cousins ceded the final drive to prized rookie Fernando Mendoza, which could be the first step toward Mendoza taking the reins. Cousins' job doesn't seem to be in immediate peril, and he could bounce back in a big way in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kirk Cousins is coming off a productive effort in the Raiders' near-upset of the Bills in Week 6, throwing for over 300 yards for the second time in six games and tossing multiple TDs for the fifth time. The veteran quarterback is on pace for his first 4,000-yard, 30-TD campaign since 2021 with the Vikings, but to reach those numbers he would need to keep first overall pick Fernando Mendoza on the bench, which looks increasingly unlikely after three straight losses for Las Vegas. Cousins will remain under center for now, but he faces another tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that is second in the league in passing yards per game allowed.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue being the main playmaker on the Falcons' offense in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson has been stellar despite Atlanta's offensive struggles three weeks into the season, accounting for 467 total yards and three touchdowns. He's already recorded 79 touches (26.3 per game) this year, suggesting this massive fantasy output will continue as the season progresses. Additionally, Robinson is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 27.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading Atlanta's offense during the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson has excelled through the Falcons' first four games, averaging 153.5 total yards per game and scoring five touchdowns on 99 touches. He ranks second in the NFL in total yards and will likely remain the focal point of a Falcons offense that's averaged 40 points per game over their last two contests. Despite this, Robinson is in for a difficult Wek 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bijan Robinson will lead Atlanta's offensive attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson remained one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 5 despite the overtime loss, totaling 128 yards on 21 touches. He ranks as the No. 3 RB in all of fantasy through five contests, averaging a whopping 26.3 points per game. He could be in for a tough Week 6 matchup, however, as Chicago's defense has given up just 18.8 fantasy points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson logged a season-low nine carries in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, as Atlanta was trailing by 24 points in the second half. Despite this, he remained productive when given the opportunities, averaging 6.8 yards per carry. Expect Robinson to bounce back and remain one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has allowed 24.5 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through five contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenneth Walker was dominant for Kansas City in the team's first four games prior to a Week 5 bye, rumbling for 537 rushing yards on 6.2 yards per carry while scoring six times-four on the ground and two through the air. Last season's Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks is earning every penny of his big free-agent contract, and his presence in the backfield is also opening things up for Patrick Mahomes, putting KC in the top five in the NFL in points per game at 29.5 and second in yards per game at 412.0, behind only the Rams. Walker should be able to continue rolling in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenneth Walker continues to shine as the new focal point of Kansas City's offense. Through his first five games with the team, Walker has piled up eight total touchdowns-six rushing and two receiving-while topping 100 rushing yards in four of those contests. He leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, despite already having had his bye and having played one fewer game than Bijan Robinson and James Cook, the only other two backs with more than 600 yards. Walker will try to deliver a revenge game in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins after undergoing minor knee surgery just before the start of the campaign. The star tight end isn't expected to be out for long, and in his absence Michael Mayer will top the team's depth chart at the position, although running back Ashton Jeanty may have been the biggest beneficiary in terms of production against Miami. If Bowers is cleared to return in Week 2, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in PPR points allowed to TEs in 2025, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Bowers is on track to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Saints after missing the Raiders' first two games due to minor knee surgery at the end of training camp. Knee trouble in 2025 prevented Bowers from repeating his dynamic rookie campaign, but if he's able to get fully healthy again, the star tight end should quickly emerge as the team's top option in the passing game, with little competition from a wide receiver room led by Tre Tucker. Bowers will initially be catching passes from Kirk Cousins, but at some point this season Las Vegas will transition to Fernando Mendoza under center, providing one more wrinkle for the offense. If he gets cleared this week as expected. Bowers will be facing a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a touchdown to a TE in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Bowers made up for lost time after missing the Raiders' first two games while recovering from minor knee surgery. In his Week 3 season debut against the Saints, the star tight end turned 13 targets into a 10-116-1 receiving line. Bowers is the clear No. 1 downfield option for Kirk Cousins, especially considering the lack of talent in the wide receiver room, and as long as he can stay healthy, he should continue to see big volume. He's in a good position to put up big numbers again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs but ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Bowers shook off an illness to once again be the Raiders' top receiving option in a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. He caught six of 11 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, finding the end zone for a second straight game after missing the first two weeks of the year while completing his recovery from knee surgery. The star tight end is the most dangerous weapon in Kirk Cousins' arsenal, and he's likely to continue getting double-digit targets on a weekly basis while posting elite numbers. Bowers faces his toughest test of the season so far in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Bowers continues to make up for lost time, producing an 8-110-1 line on 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After missing the first two games of the season while completing his recovery from knee surgery, the superstar tight end has gotten into the end zone in three straight weeks, amassing 24 catches for 312 yards and three scores on 35 targets. Bowers is the clear top option for Kirk Cousins in the passing game, and that isn't likely to change even if Las Vegas eventually switches to rookie Fernando Mendoza under center. Bowers will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Bowers was held somewhat in check by the Bills in Week 6, failing to get double-digit targets for the first time in 2026 and managing a 4-70-0 line on nine looks from Kirk Cousins. Fellow TE Michael Mayer popped for a big game, but Bowers probably won't stay contained for long. Over his four appearances this season, Bowers has a 28-382-3 line on 44 targets as the clear top option in the Raiders' passing game. He'll face a tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emeka Egbuka will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Egbuka was targeted just four times during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, his lowest mark of the season. While Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined and Jalon Daniels acts as the Buccaneers' signal caller, Egbuka may continue receiving less opportunities. However, he's in for a great Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's given up 36.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Egbuka had a good bounce-back performance in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching six of nine targets for 38 yards while adding 14 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Despite a relatively underwhelming start to the season, Egbuka still leads Tampa Bay in yards (192), targets (33) and receptions (21) through five games. He could struggle in Week 6 against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed just 27.7 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Egbuka had his most promising game of the 2026 season in the overtime loss to the Steelers, turning a whopping 16 targets into seven receptions for 48 yards and a score. Tampa Bay's offense has struggled without Baker Mayfield (thumb), averaging just 167 passing yards per game since his injury. Despite this, Egbuka has remained productive and could benefit from the potential return of Mayfield in Week 7. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka could struggle against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: Terry McLaurin had a rough Week 1 for the Commanders. On only four targets, McLaurin caught a mere two passes for 14 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. It will be interesting to see if the presence of Diggs in particular impacts McLaurin, as Diggs more than doubled McLaurin in targets with nine. Both wideouts should see plenty of action in Week 2 versus a poor Cowboys defense, though. Dallas allowed 229 passing yards and three touchdowns through the air to Jaxson Dart in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Terry McLaurin is coming off his best game of the season for the Commanders. Scary Terry had six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown in the shocking 33-31 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. McLaurin has posted nine targets in back-to-back contests.  McLaurin caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Terry McLaurin missed last game for the Commanders due to a hamstring injury. McLaurin allegedly pushed hard to play, though, meaning he could very well return to the field in Week 5 versus the Giants. He also could have his starting quarterback Jayden Daniels back under center. New York has been stingy against the pass in 2026 thus far, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. Likewise, the G-Men are tied for the league-lead with six picks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Montgomery scored three total TDs in his Texans debut in Week 1 and profiles as a borderline fantasy RB1 for a Week 2 home game against a Bengals defense that gave up 93 scrimmage yards and a score to Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving. Montgomery had 23 touches to Woody Marks' 10 in Week 1 against the Bills, so the former Lions RB is operating as the clear lead back for his new team. Montgomery's 23 Week 1 touches were more than he had in any game last season with Detroit. Cincinnati beefed up its defensive front in the offseason after allowing the most rushing yards in the NFL last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: David Montgomery produced just 24 scrimmage yards in Houston's Week 2 loss to the Bengals after scoring three TDs in his Texans debut. The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: David Montgomery is averaging a paltry 2.8 yards per carry, and Houston's offensive line has struggled to open up holes heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The offseason trade acquisition scored three TDs in his Texans' debut but hasn't found the end zone since. Through three games, Montgomery has out-touched Woody Marks 44-29, but Marks scored a one-yard touchdown in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, so Montgomery doesn't have a monopoly on short-yardage opportunities. The Cowboys are allowing 27.3 points per game and have surrendered four total TDs to RBs, so Montgomery is a fantasy RB2 for Week 4, albeit a touchdown-dependent one.
outlooksByWeek.5: David Montgomery has plodded to 2.7 yards per carry and has failed to find the end zone since scoring three TDs in Week 1, his Texans debut. Fellow Houston RB Woody Marks has scored twice during Montgomery's three-game touchdown drought. Montgomery and Marks will likely split carries again in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 100 rushing yards per game to RBs, though Tennessee is giving up only 3.6 yards per carry. If Houston's defense can recapture last season's elite form and stifle the underwhelming Titans offense, Montgomery could get enough volume to wear down Tennessee's defense and make up for a lack of quality with quantity. With Houston's running game stuck in first gear, Montgomery is an unexciting flex candidate for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: David Montgomery is considered week-to-week after departing Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans due to a groin injury. He's likely to sit out in Week 6 against the Jaguars, leaving Woody Marks to lead Houston's backfield against Jacksonville's league-best run defense in London. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: David Montgomery (groin) sat out Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars and is considered week-to-week. If he returns for Week 7 against the Giants, Montgomery would likely split carries with Woody Marks and possibly Jawhar Jordan. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry. The Giants have struggled to defend RBs, allowing 108 rushing yards and one total TD per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxson Dart was electric in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing for an additional 54 yards in the stunning 28-20 win over the Cowboys. Dart threw just five incompletions and showed excellent rapport with new tight end Isaiah Likely. Dart was accurate, decisive and poised in what amounted to an extremely promising start to the season for the G-Men. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Los Angeles Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in their opener, allowing 379 scrimmage yards, which ranks them in the bottom third of the NFL. The Rams were torched on the ground in particular to the tune of 174 yards. While Myles Garrett will be sidelined due to a knee injury, the Rams will get Aaron Donald back from retirement when they host the Giants on Monday Night Football.

player.seasonOutlook: Dart is a strong 2026 breakout candidate following an impressive rookie campaign in which he delivered eight top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for fifth most) despite playing the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games. Dart was solid as a passer but elite as a rusher, finishing in the top five at the position in rushing attempts, yards, TDs and carries inside the 5-yard line. Dart's aggressive playing style raises concerns about his durability, but it also provides the 23-year-old with elite fantasy upside. With a new coaching staff led by John Harbaugh and a new playcaller in Matt Nagy, as well as an improved supporting cast that includes a healthy Malik Nabers and newcomers Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney, Dart is best valued as a midrange QB1 with a high ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Thomas tied for second on the Jaguars with 40 receiving yards on three targets in the season opener, as Trevor Lawrence threw just 21 passes in a lopsided win over the Browns. Fellow WRs Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both got into the end zone, while Thomas failed to score. Thomas also left the game to be evaluated for a shoulder injury, though he managed to return. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, and the team's entire offensive output could be limited in a Week 2 road matchup against a Denver defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the NFL last season and employs star CB Patrick Surtain. Given that context, Thomas is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Thomas has played fewer than 40% of Jacksonville's offensive snaps in two of the team's first three games while totaling just 88 yards. He has been outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the Jaguars' WR room, which leaves Thomas as a risky fantasy option in Week 4 against the Bengals. Benching the struggling Thomas is a defensible move, though he still maintains starter-worthy upside here considering Thomas flashed elite talent en route to an 87-1,282-10 line as a rookie in 2024, and the Bengals just allowed three different Steelers wideouts to score in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brian Thomas has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last two games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has played fewer than 50% of snaps on offense while being outperformed by Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers. Thomas is too talented to overlook completely, but he's a risky flex option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London. The matchup would become more favorable if Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) sits. Philadelphia is allowing 162 receiving yards per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brian Thomas is coming off a Week 5 goose egg against the Eagles and has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last three games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has a snap share below 50% this season heading into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to defend WRs, allowing 193 yards per game to the position, but Thomas isn't a trustworthy fantasy option despite the favorable matchup given his recent struggles. Unless you are desperate for a bye-week plug-in in a deeper format, Thomas should be left on the bench if not dropped outright.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center. Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: J.K. Dobbins is coming off his largest workload of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams. He had 17 carries and 18 total touches but turned them into just 53 scrimmage yards. Dobbins has struggled out of the gate, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but he should continue to handle the majority of the early-down work while rookie Jonah Coleman is on IR. RJ Harvey, who compiled 47 scrimmage yards on just eight touches against the Rams, remains the primary passing-down back. Dobbins will look for his first touchdown of 2026 in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: J.K. Dobbins continues to struggle as the primary early-down back for the Broncos. In a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, he managed just 40 rushing yards on 11 carries. This marks the fourth straight game to begin the season he's failed to reach 50 rushing yards or get into the end zone. Dobbins' 3.5 yards per carry would be a career low; he's never had a mark below 4.6 in any year he's played at least eight games. The veteran RB has at least stayed healthy, but that hasn't led to much production. He'll try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: J.K. Dobbins scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, while also producing season highs in touches (20) and rushing yards (68). The veteran running back was one of the few players to clearly benefit from Sean Payton's return to play-calling duties, but Dobbins still managed fairly modest numbers. He's been able to stay healthy so far in 2026, but through five games he's averaged just 3.6 yards per carry, a mark that would be a career low if it doesn't improve. Dobbins will take on a Seahawks defense in Week 6 that's tied for 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but which has yet to allow any back to reach 70 rushing yards in a game.
outlooksByWeek.7: J.K. Dobbins scored a rushing touchdown for a second straight game in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran running back hasn't found much success overall in a struggling offense, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry with zero gains of 20-plus yards through six games, but his role as the goal-line back provides him with a consistent path to production. Dobbins is also more involved as a pass catcher in recent weeks, producing an 8-27-0 line while logging multiple targets in four straight weeks. He'll look to break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 28th in rushing yards per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

player.seasonOutlook: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 targets (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine mid-round upside pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen McMillan (knee) will operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options if active for the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. McMillan was unable to suit up in Week 1 due to a nagging knee injury, but he could have a valuable role in Tampa Bay's receiving corps once healthy. Outside of Emeka Egbuka, the Buccaneers' wideouts combined to catch seven of eight targets for 76 yards in Week 1, which suggests McMillan will have a large opportunity to contribute when available. He's in for a great Week 2 matchup as well, with Cleveland's defense allowing three touchdowns to WRs last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Loop and the Ravens look to keep rolling at home versus the Saints in Week 2. Baltimore put up 41 points in their Week 1 victory, and Loop was a perfect 7-for-7 on his attempts. He made all five PATs and drilled both field-goal attempts-one from 57 yards out and one from 45. As long as he's the starting kicker, Loop should see plenty of scoring chances in this high-scoring Ravens offense. He'll try to stay perfect against a New Orleans defense that gave up 31 points to the Lions in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the Cowboys for a Week 3 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on both PATs during Baltimore's 24-17 loss in Week 2. Loop's first attempt from 49 yards was blocked, but he followed up by making his second attempt from the same distance. He should have plenty of opportunities to score in what's expected to be a high-scoring contest versus Dallas inside the AT&T Stadium dome in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Loop and the Ravens return home to square off against the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was perfect again in Baltimore's dramatic 34-31 victory in Brazil in Week 3, making both of his field-goal attempts, including a 56-yard game-winning kick as time expired, and all four of his extra points. Loop is now 5-for-6 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-11 on extra-point tries in 2026. The Ravens are fifth in scoring at 30.7 points per game, so he should continue earning plenty of opportunities for one of the best offenses in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Loop and the Ravens pay a visit to the surging Falcons for a Week 5 interconference clash on Sunday Night Football. The second-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on all three PATs during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. Loop missed his second field goal of the season but set a new career high with his make from 64 yards out, and he's now 6-for-8 on field goals and a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points. Atlanta has scored the most points in the league over its last two games (80), meaning Loop and the Ravens will have to keep up in a potential high-scoring game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Loop and the Ravens travel to square off against the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime victory in Week 5. Two of Loop's makes came from 50-plus yards, and he's now 5-for-5 on kicks from that distance this season and 9-for-11 on field goals overall. He's turning into a very reliable fantasy asset for a Ravens team that scores 29.2 points per game, making him a strong play against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Loop and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals for a Week 7 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Through six contests this season, Loop is 10-for-13 (76.9%) on field goals and a perfect 16-for-16 on extra-point tries. He has three outings with 100% accuracy and three with 50% accuracy, making him an inconsistent fantasy option despite kicking for a Ravens offense that scores 26.0 points per game, which ranks seventh so far in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to come out of the bye week with a bang as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Gibbs was a monster in Week 5 against the Cardinals, rushing 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns, with five catches for 56 yards as well. The premier running back has now surpassed 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season, and he's found the end zone nine times across five games. He'll face a Green Bay front that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Breece Hall will look to remain busy when the Jets face the Packers in Week 2. Hall handled 24 total touches to open the year, finishing with 118 total yards and a touchdown-an encouraging start under new OC Frank Reich. The Packers allowed just 3.7 yards per carry last week but did give up two rushing scores. Much of Hall's volume came in a favorable game script, something that may not repeat in Week 2, but with better than a 2:1 touch split with Braelon Allen, Hall will garner ample opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.
outlooksByWeek.4: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Bears in the Jets' Week 4 matchup due to a thigh injury. Hall has struggled over the last two weeks, gaining just 61 yards on 29 carries, but his workload in the passing game has been steady. Should he play, Hall has an inviting matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.9 yards per carry. Braelon Allen would likely lead the backfield in the event of Hall's absence, with Isaiah Davis playing second fiddle.
outlooksByWeek.5: Breece Hall is uncertain to face the Browns in the Jets' Week 5 matchup due to a quad injury. He missed Week 4 with the issue, and when healthy, he was limited to 32 or fewer yards in his last two outings. Should he suit up, it's possible he'd be eased into his return and share snaps with Braelon Allen, but it's a favorable spot if a normal workload can be anticipated. While Cleveland has yet to allow a running back to score, they're allowing 4.8 yards per carry, with the last three lead backs all reaching at least 82 yards.
outlooksByWeek.6: Breece Hall needs to overcome a quad injury to suit up for the first time in three weeks when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Braelon Allen has shouldered the load in Hall's absence, and a split workload can be anticipated once Hall returns. Hall would require an unlikely heavy volume to be a top option facing a New England defense that's allowed just 399 rushing yards through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Breece Hall has missed three straight games due to a quad injury as the Jets get set to face the Dolphins in Week 7. Braelon Allen has shined during Hall's absence, and should Hall be deemed healthy, it would appear safe to assume he'd be eased back into action. Miami's defense ranks in the middle of the pack against opposing rushers, allowing 4.0 yards per carry and three rushing scores, but five touchdowns through the air to opposing backs. With questionable volume if he returns to action, it's probably wise to wait one more week before deploying Hall.

player.seasonOutlook: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.4: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Davante Adams is coming off his second two-TD game of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 6 battle versus Arizona. Against Buffalo on Monday Night Football in Week 5, Adams recorded a 5-51-2 line on seven targets. While he lagged far behind Puka Nacua's 24 targets and massive 17-138-1 line, Adams continued to work as a top option for QB Matthew Stafford in the red zone.
