outlooksByWeek.6: Parker Washington bounced back from a seven-yard Week 4 dud with his best game of the season in Week 5, racking up 124 yards and two TDs against the Eagles. Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver is averaging 70 yards per game and has four TDs through five outings while leading the Jaguars in every receiving category. Washington can be penciled in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 6 against a Texans pass defense that has been surprisingly weak, allowing 193 receiving yards per game to wideouts and six TDs in five games to the position, making it one of the five most generous defenses against wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dallas Goedert was the leading receiver for the Eagles in Week 1. Goedert snagged four passes for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-22 win over Washington. Goedert was targeted five times. With A.J. Brown no longer in the fold, Goedert could see even more touches in the red zone. In Week 2, the Eagles will face the Tennessee Titans.  Tennessee was a tad frisky against the pass in Week 1, allowing just 215 yards passing to the Jets.  In addition, the Titans did not allow a passing touchdown for the game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dallas Goedert did not suit up last game for the Eagles due to a knee injury, and his status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. In his place, Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt combined for just two catches for 13 yards. Even if Goedert can suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.2 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dallas Goedert missed last game for the Eagles with a knee issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Goedert misses additional time, Zach Ertz would be the next man up.  An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dallas Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions last game. Returning from a two-game absence due to a knee injury, Goedert responded with six catches on nine targets. Unfortunately, Goedert gained just 38 yards, and the Eagles lost by a score of 19-17. If both DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley continue to be sidelined due to their respective hamstring injuries, though, Goedert should see plenty of looks, including in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dallas Goedert caught six passes for 61 yards last game for the Eagles. Goedert was second on the team in targets behind DeVonta Smith. Even with Tanner McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Goedert should still have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Worthy captured three of his six Week 1 targets for only 18 yards. The workload was low, but Kansas City QB Patrick Mahomes completed only five passes to wideouts in the Monday night opener. The third-year pro has the speed to stretch the field, but he's generally used more underneath, along with occasionally carrying the ball. Worthy is a Week 2 flex option when the Chiefs host the Colts. Indianapolis was one of five defenses to allow over 300 yards passing in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Worthy comes out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye still looking to establish himself as a consistent part of the passing attack. With both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton getting hurt during a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Worthy caught four of seven targets for a season-high 70 yards. Rice appears to be on track to return quickly, but Thornton is likely to miss the rest of the year, which could open up some downfield routes for Worthy. The third-year speedster will face a Chargers secondary in Week 6 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Worthy is coming off his most productive game of the season, catching all seven of his targets for 73 yards in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers. With Rashee Rice sidelined, Worthy's volume has ticked up, but he hasn't been targeted more than seven times in a game this season. The third-year speedster also hasn't been able to break many big gains, with only one of his 21 catches going for 20-plus yards after nine of his 42 receptions in 2025 went for 20-plus. Worthy isn't likely to produce a ceiling game in Week 7 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing as a rookie with 101 touches and 12 touchdowns in 20 games (including the playoffs), Worthy had the look of an emerging star. Things didn't go as planned in Year 2, though, as the 2024 first-round pick was injured on his third snap of the season and wasn't productive or utilized as much as expected upon his return. Worthy was limited to one touchdown (Week 6) and reached 12 fantasy points once in 14 games (Week 4). The speedy Worthy is still only 23 years old, so a Year 3 breakout is certainly possible, especially with Rashee Rice and 36-year-old Travis Kelce as his only legit target competition. He's worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dalton Kincaid faces an uphill battle for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Rams in Week 5. He is coming off a season-low seven yards on two targets (one catch), and after a productive two-game start, has only five targets in Weeks 3 and 4. The Rams have defended tight ends at an elite level, allowing a mere 2.9 yards per target and only 85 total yards through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills' passing game is shrinking ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. After snagging 12 of 14 targets in his first two games, Kincaid has been limited to four catches on seven targets over the last three weeks, amassing just 52 yards. His snap share remains strong and elevated from 2025; Buffalo just seems more inclined to be a run-first offense. Las Vegas has allowed six touchdowns to opposing tight ends, resulting in the fifth-most fantasy points allowed to the position. Kincaid can be a viable starting option in a favorable bounce-back matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 2 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's now been placed on IR for the injury. The fifth-year running back (30 of 65 offensive snaps) and Aaron Jones (29 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps against the Packers, with Mason leading the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Unfortunately, Mason will now be out for at least the next four weeks, priming Jones for a bigger role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 4 as the Vikings take on the Dolphins. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next two weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Mason will remain out for Week 5 as the Vikings travel to New Orleans. Mason hurt his thumb in Week 1 against the Packers, and he's been on IR since. The fifth-year running back will remain sidelined for at least the next week, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Mason could be set to return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Mason has been sidelined since Week 1 with a thumb injury that landed him on IR, but he's set to return to practice this week. The fifth-year running back's return should put him at least in a complementary role with veteran Aaron Jones. Indianapolis' defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Jones is unlikely to post gaudy passing numbers in the Colts' run-first offense, and he doesn't appear interested in using his legs as much after tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of last season. His fantasy appeal is limited to multi-QB or superflex formats, and Jones is a low-end option even in those leagues for a Week 2 matchup against a Chiefs defense that held Bo Nix to 131 passing yards in Week 1. Jones had just 166 passing yards with a 1:1 TD:INT and one carry for four yards in the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Ravens.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Jones is averaging 188 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 3 home game against the Texans. Houston gave up two touchdown passes apiece to star QBs Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, but Jones will be hard-pressed to post his first multi-TD performance of the season considering the Texans boast one of the league's best defenses, having allowed the fewest yards in the NFL last season. The Colts will continue to rely primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and Indianapolis has an underwhelming group of pass catchers that's expected to be without last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel) for several weeks. Jones has been a non-factor as a rusher since returning from a torn Achilles, with just 14 rushing yards this season. His mediocre passing stats make him an unappealing Week 3 fantasy option, even in multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.4: Daniel Jones led the Colts to their first win since Week 10 of the 2025 season in Week 3 against the Texans, but he has just three touchdown passes and five turnovers heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Jones, who underwent surgery to repair a torn Achilles in December, hasn't been much of a factor with his legs, rushing for just 19 yards and has yet to score a rushing TD after notching five last season. Washington has allowed a league-high 11 passing TDs, so while Jones will be tough to trust as a starter in one-QB formats with the Colts missing last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel; IR), he's a viable option in superflex or multi-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.5: Daniel Jones is averaging 189 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 5 trip to Pittsburgh. Jones threw for a season-high 342 yards against the Steelers last season but had five turnovers in that game. His passing production is likely to be much more muted in this rematch while throwing to a depleted Colts receiving corps that remains without Alec Pierce (heel; IR) and played without Keenan Allen (groin) in the Week 4 win over the Commanders in London. Pittsburgh's defense has limited QBs to a 5:4 TD:INT, while Jones has an even worse 3:4 TD:INT this season. Even superflex and multi-QB league managers are better off looking elsewhere.
outlooksByWeek.6: Daniel Jones has just a 3:4 TD:INT and hasn't rushed for more than 10 yards in a game heading into the Colts' Week 6 home game against the Titans. Indianapolis' offense relies primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and that formula is unlikely to change since the Colts will likely have the luxury of playing from ahead in Week 6 against a Titans team that has been outscored 109-58 this season but allowed only five passing TDs. Between Jones' own limitations as a passer and his team's lack of receiving talent, he remains an unappetizing Week 6 fantasy option, even in superflex and multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Daniel Jones and the Colts are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the previously winless Titans, and things get significantly more difficult on the road in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game. Jones played his part in the loss to Tennessee with a season-worst two interceptions, and he has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game while posting a 4:6 TD:INT through six outings. He's averaging just 215 passing yards and nine rushing yards per game. Even in superflex and multi-QB formats, the struggling QB isn't an advisable fantasy option.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones re-signed with the Colts during the offseason and will return as the team's starter. The 2019 No. 6 draft pick made a big leap in 2025 -- his first season with Indianapolis -- finishing no lower than seventh in completion percentage and yards per attempt. Despite the strong play, Jones was inconsistent as a fantasy option, averaging 18.8 fantasy points during 12 full games and posting three top-five weeks but no additional finishes better than ninth. Jones was effective through the air and scored five rushing TDs, but he didn't run the ball as much as in years past and might do even less of that in 2026 after tearing an Achilles in Week 14. He's likely to be ready for Week 1, but effectiveness is a concern, so he's best viewed as a midrange QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Rodriguez had just six carries to Bhayshul Tuten's 15 in Jacksonville's season opener. Considering Rodriguez contributes almost nothing as a pass-catcher, with just six receptions in 36 career games, he'll be nothing more than a touchdown-dependent deep-league dart throw for fantasy purposes as long as Tuten is healthy. Rodriguez is unlikely to find the end zone in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the second-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing TDs (eight) to RBs last season, though Denver gave up two total TDs to Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Rodriguez has notched just six rushing attempts in each of his first two games with the Jaguars. He's averaging a paltry 3.0 yards per carry and has yet to earn a target in the passing game, where Rodriguez has been a non-factor his entire NFL career. Bhayshul Tuten has 28 carries this season and is the clear lead back for the Jaguars. Rodriguez isn't an advisable fantasy play in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing a minuscule 8.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first three games with the Jaguars heading into a Week 4 road tilt at Cincinnati. He scored his first TD of the season in the Week 3 rout of the Patriots, but Rodriguez will remain a touchdown-dependent deep-league option as long as Bhayshul Tuten is available. The Bengals have allowed the most receiving yards in the league to RBs, but Rodriguez almost certainly won't capitalize on that weakness, as he has yet to earn a target this year and has just six career catches in 38 games.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Rodriguez has a consistent role as the Jaguars' No. 2 RB behind Bhayshul Tuten, but Rodriguez's usage level is too low to warrant lineup consideration in most formats. Rodriguez has recorded between six and eight carries in each of his first four games with the Jaguars. He's riding a two-game TD streak but has been a complete non-factor in the passing game with zero targets while averaging a mediocre 4.2 yards per carry. Jacksonville faces an Eagles defense in Week 5 that ranks among the 10 most generous to RBs on the ground, allowing 106 rushing yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Rodriguez has exceeded six rushing attempts in only one of five games with the Jaguars and has just one catch all season. With starting RB Bhayshul Tuten healthy heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans, Rodriguez doesn't look like a usable fantasy option in most formats against a stout Houston front seven that's limiting RBs to 3.5 yards per carry. Rodriguez remains a viable bench stash for managers hedging against a Tuten injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodriguez, a 2023 sixth-round NFL draft pick, spent his first three seasons with Washington and has primarily played a depth role, but he did hit career-high marks in touches (115), yardage (530) and touchdowns (six) in 2025. Rodriguez has handled more than 10 touches in nine career games and averaged 13.1 touches, 65.9 yards and 11.7 fantasy points with a total of seven touchdowns in those outings. Though he's an effective rusher, Rodriguez is not an option in the passing game (seven career targets). The 26-year-old's contract included a healthy $6.2 million in guarantees, so he's likely to have a legitimate offensive role as a counterpart to second-year backs Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen Jr. Rodriguez might score the occasional touchdown, but his role won't allow consistent fantasy output. He's best stashed on benches.

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harrison Mevis is coming off a quiet season opener as the Rams prepare to face the Giants in Week 2. Los Angeles' offense was held by the 49ers to just seven points last Thursday, and Mevis didn't get the opportunity to attempt any field goals. The Rams figure to be much more prolific on that side of the ball most weeks, so Mevis should be more active moving forward, though last year he attempted 39 PATs to just 13 field goals. The Giants' defense put up a good performance in a Week 1 win over Dallas, with star kicker Brandon Aubrey getting no field-goal tries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harrison Mevis is still searching for his first field-goal conversion heading into the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Mevis didn't try a FG in Week 1, and he missed his only attempt -- a 43-yarder -- on Monday Night Football. Mevis did make all four of his extra-point tries and figures to kick a lot of those given the Rams' explosive offense. Kickers have gone 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts against the Broncos so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harrison Mevis is coming off a career-best four FGs ahead of the Rams' matchup versus Philadelphia in Week 4. After going 0-for-1 in field-goal tries over the first two weeks of the campaign, Mevis was asked to attempt four FGs versus Denver in Week 3 and made every try, including a 48-yarder. With that said, the Rams' explosive offense doesn't frequently end drives with field-goal attempts, so Mevis may struggle to see such volume moving forward. Opponents have been successful on five of six field-goal attempts versus the Eagles so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Harrison Mevis heads into the Rams' Week 5 matchup against Buffalo with a modest four field goals on the season. Four of those came in Week 3 against Denver, and Mevis missed a 48-yard try this past Sunday against Philadelphia. The second-year pro is a perfect 10-for-10 on point-after tries this year and has made all 49 of his PAT attempts in his career. Buffalo has yielded just six FG tries through four weeks, with kickers making five of those attempts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Harrison Mevis' job may be on the line heading into the Rams' Week 6 contest against the Cardinals. Mevis missed both of his field-goal attempts in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, including a 50-yarder in the first quarter and a blocked 48-yarder in overtime that could have won the game. He's now just 5-for-9 on FG tries this season, including 3-for-6 from 40-to-49 yards out. Should Mevis still be kicking for the Rams in Week 6, he may be limited mostly to extra points versus a Cardinals defense that has yielded 18 PAT tries to just six FG attempts this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to face the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Week 4 before leaving Cincinnati's 22-17 loss with a concussion in the second quarter. Chase was evaluated for the injury after his facemask was pulled following a catch, and he'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to practice and play in the upcoming contest versus Miami. If he is indeed active, Chase will be going up against the Dolphins, who rank third in fewest fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are on the road for an AFC North showdown against the Ravens in Week 7. He corralled six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to pace his team in all receiving categories, as no other Bengal had more than 25 yards or four targets. He'll once again be the primary offensive threat for Joe Burrow versus the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Derrick Henry and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 5 clash against the Falcons. He tallied 23 carries for 73 yards and one touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 4 victory. Henry notched his seventh rushing TD of the season and now has at least one score in all four outings. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status up in the air, Henry should continue to be the focal point of the Ravens' offense versus Atlanta's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.9) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a divisional clash in Week 6. He rushed 24 times for 102 yards and caught one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. The game marked Henry's first scoreless outing on the ground in 2026, and he draws a difficult Week 6 matchup against a Browns' defense that has surrendered just one combined TD to the position. Cleveland ranks seventh by allowing 17.6 fantasy points per game to RBs, but the Jets' Braelon Allen racked up 116 rushing yards and one score on 24 attempts in Week 5. The Browns could again be without two starters on the defensive line, and with Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question, Henry has another opportunity to be the primary engine of the offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Derrick Henry and the Ravens welcome the Bengals to town for a divisional clash in Week 7. He rushed 17 times for 58 yards and caught his lone target for two yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6, also losing a costly fumble in the fourth quarter. The outing marked Henry's first this season without a touchdown, and his 60 scrimmage yards were his lowest output through six games. He will aim to bounce back at home in Week 7 versus a Cincinnati defense that allows 19.0 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury. He paced Houston's passing attack with a 7-75-1 line on 10 targets in the season opener, so he would work as the team's WR1 again in Week 2 against the Bengals if given the green light to suit up. Cincinnati didn't allow a passing TD to the Buccaneers in Week 1 but had one of the league's worst all-around defenses last season, when the Bengals gave up the second-most yards and third-most points in the NFL. Collins remains a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 as he chases his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nico Collins (hamstring) didn't suit up for the Texans in Week 2 and may not be ready to return against the Colts in Week 3. If Collins recovers, he'll jump back in as the top option in Houston's passing game and a fantasy WR2 at worst. Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nico Collins (hamstring) could return from a two-week absence in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Houston's No. 1 WR will immediately jump back into the fantasy WR1 range if he plays against a Dallas defense that's giving up 27.3 points per game. The Cowboys have allowed seven touchdowns through the air, though only three of those went to WRs. Houston hasn't garnered much production out of its wide receiver room in Collins' absence. If Collins remains unavailable, TE Dalton Schultz would likely remain the de facto top target for QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nico Collins returned from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury in Week 5 and reclaimed his customary spot as Houston's top receiver and a fantasy WR1. He scored twice against the Cowboys and has compiled 14 catches for 194 yards and three TDs in two appearances this season. Collins can be started with confidence in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 167 receiving yards per game to wideouts. DeVonta Smith and Zay Flowers each compiled at least 117 yards and a TD against Tennessee's secondary.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nico Collins is averaging 83 receiving yards and one touchdown per game as the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game. His role isn't expected to change in Week 6 against the Jaguars, even with the Texans having traded for 2024 fourth overall pick Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Jacksonville boasts the league's best run defense but has a vulnerable secondary, as the Jaguars are the only team to have allowed over 1,000 yards to wide receivers this season. Collins is a top-five fantasy WR for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Nico Collins has posted at least 79 scrimmage yards in three of his four appearances this season for the Texans ahead of a Week 7 home game against the Giants. The star wideout can be deployed in his usual spot as a fantasy WR1 for Week 7 while facing a Giants secondary that has done a decent job of suppressing yards from WRs but is tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to the position with seven. Collins has 24 touchdown receptions in 46 games since the start of the 2023 campaign, including three scores in four games this season as the top target for resurgent QB C.J. Stroud.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bucky Irving is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' lead back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Irving out-touched Kenneth Gainwell 15 to six in the Week 1 loss, which is a very promising sign for his outlook moving forward. The most impressive part about Irving's Week 1 performance was receiving, where he caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards. He could be in for another big week against a Browns defense that allowed 34 points in Week 1. However, Cleveland did give up just 3.9 yards per carry, so Irving may need to continue his success as a receiver for fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bucky Irving is expected to remain Tampa Bay's lead back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Irving remained efficient despite the Buccaneers' offensive struggles in Week 2, accounting for 90 total yards on 21 touches. Additionally, he's operated as the clear No. 1 running back, out-touching Kenneth Gainwell 36 to 11 in two contests. Irving will likely struggle in Week 3, however, as he'll be facing a Vikings defense that's allowed just 14.7 PPR fantasy points to RBs this season, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bucky Irving is expected to continue leading the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Irving was held in check by a strong Vikings defense in Week 3, totaling 58 yards on 17 touches. Despite this inefficient effort, Irving remained the Buccaneers' bell-cow back, as Kenneth Gainwell received just five touches (10 total yards). With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dealing with injury following the Week 3 loss, Irving could see less opportunities through the air. Regardless, Irving's strong workload should bode well for the Week 4 matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed the second-most PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position (30.7) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the Buccaneers' main offensive weapon in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Irving was largely ineffective against the Packers in a Week 4 loss, rushing for 61 yards on 16 carries. Additionally, the Oregon product was held without a target after accumulating 15 in Tampa Bay's first three games, suggesting Irving is likely in for less pass-catching opportunities while Jalon Daniels remains the starting quarterback. Irving could still thrive in Week 5 against a Cowboys defense that's given up 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Irving was phenomenal in the Week 5 upset win over the Cowboys, totaling 175 yards and two touchdowns on 23 touches. Despite this, Irving is seeing less receiving work since Jalon Daniels took over for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback, getting just three targets over his last two games. Even so, Irving should remain productive in Week 6 against a Steelers defense that's allowed 22.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Irving was relatively quiet in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, totaling 49 yards on 22 touches. Despite this, he remains firmly ahead of Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker in Tampa Bay's backfield and could thrive in Week 7, as Carolina's defense has allowed 25.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season. Additionally, Irving could benefit from the possible return of quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb), as Irving averaged 5.0 targets per game while Mayfield was healthy (just 2.0 since Mayfield's injury).

player.seasonOutlook: Irving enters his third season coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he missed seven games and struggled with efficiency. After averaging 5.42 yards per carry and producing 1,514 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, Irving fell to 3.40 YPC (fourth worst among qualified RBs), 865 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He failed to clear 4.2 YPC in any of his 10 outings and had zero carries inside the opponent's 5 yard line. The 24-year-old remains positioned as the lead back in Tampa Bay, but the combination of his small frame (5-foot-9, 192 pounds) and the arrival of Kenneth Gainwell (not to mention Sean Tucker at the goal line) suggest he might play a lesser role moving forward. Irving should be valued as a back-end RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit the Texans for a Week 2 battle between two playoff hopefuls. He caught three of six targets for 59 yards during Cincinnati's season-opening victory. Higgins tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing behind Mike Gesicki for the lead in receiving yards. He draws a favorable matchup against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to take on their division rivals in Week 3. He finished Week 2's win over Houston with five catches on 10 targets for 95 yards, pacing Cincinnati in yardage and targets. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, and that's likely to remain the case despite an unfavorable Week 3 matchup. The Steelers' defense ranks second in fantasy points allowed per game (15.5) and has yet to surrender a TD to WRs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home to host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He tallied six catches for 90 yards and one TD on seven targets during Cincinnati's tough 30-27 loss in Week 3. Higgins was second on the team in receptions, yardage, and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase, but he led the way with 15.0 yards per catch. He'll aim to keep rolling against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (31.5) and 27th in yards per target to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are on the road to take on Miami's third-ranked defense against wide receivers in Week 5. He erupted for 11 catches and 157 yards on 16 targets during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) exiting in the second quarter, Joe Burrow relied heavily on Higgins, as he paced the team in yardage and targets while tying for the lead in receptions. Unfortunately for the Bengals, Higgins sustained an adductor injury in the final minutes of the game, leaving his status questionable for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tee Higgins and the Bengals travel to Baltimore for a divisional clash in Week 7. He caught two of four targets for 22 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Higgins was able to battle through an adductor injury that kept him limited in practices leading up to the contest, and he has now had a bye week for some added rest. He draws a favorable matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 34.1 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 22nd.

player.seasonOutlook: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trevor Lawrence is off to an inconsistent start this season, with seven touchdown passes in two home games but just one touchdown pass in two road games. The Jaguars are the nominal home team in Week 5 against the Eagles, but the game will be played in London at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium rather than in Jacksonville. Given Lawrence's struggles away from home coupled with a matchup against an Eagles defense that has allowed just four touchdown passes in as many games, this could be a week to look elsewhere at QB if a viable alternative is available on your bench or waiver wire. Jacksonville's passing game has enough upside for Lawrence to deliver a starter-level performance, but his floor is well below that.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trevor Lawrence threw for a season-high 331 yards against the Eagles as the Jaguars improved to 4-1 with a Week 5 win. He brings a 10:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans, which will be the Jaguars' second consecutive game in London. Houston has surprisingly been one of the league's most generous pass defenses, allowing QBs to throw for 256 yards per game, though the Texans have allowed only six TDs through the air. Lawrence produced just 380 passing yards with a 1:2 TD:INT in two meetings with the AFC South rival Texans in 2025, but since Houston's defense has taken a step back this season, Lawrence can continue to be deployed as a starting fantasy QB for Week 6.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wan'Dale Robinson is averaging just 35 receiving yards per game for the Titans heading into a Week 6 road affair against the Colts, who are allowing 160 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Robinson has drawn at least five targets from Cam Ward in all but one game this season, and his steady involvement makes him a viable flex play for Week 6 against the Colts' beatable pass defense. However, Robinson's ceiling is capped due to the poor play of Tennessee's entire offense, which ranks last leaguewide with 11.6 points per game. Two of Ward's three touchdown passes through five games have gone to Robinson.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wan'Dale Robinson drew 30 targets from Titans QB Cam Ward over the past four games. Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll loved peppering Robinson with short targets when they were together on the Giants, and Daboll has maintained that philosophy in their new surroundings. Robinson has caught 19 of those 30 targets for 151 yards and two TDs, and his consistent involvement in Tennessee's offense gives him a respectable floor as a solid Week 7 flex option against the Browns, who are giving up 157 yards per game to WRs and have allowed seven TDs to the position through six games. Robinson and QB Cam Ward are the only Titans with multiple TDs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has been extremely productive for Carolina over its last three games, averaging 120 yards and a touchdown per game on 73 total touches. While Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on the injured reserve list, Hubbard is expected to continue taking the vast majority of work in the Panthers' backfield. Despite this, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slated to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on his tight ends in the past. The Bucs have allowed 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season, 31st in the lerague.
outlooksByWeek.4: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins. Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.
outlooksByWeek.5: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if they're underperforming.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Bates will seek to stay perfect as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Bates has now drilled both of his two field-goal attempts and all eight of his PATs this season. The third-year kicker hasn't been on the field for many field goals this season, and Detroit playing from behind doesn't help his case. Luckily, the team's current high volume of touchdowns has kept Bates relevant. He'll face a New York squad that's allowed 6.0 points per game to kickers across two games, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Bates will look to stay perfect as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. Bates nailed his sole extra-point attempt and all four of his XPAs in Week 3 against the Jets. The third-year boot has now converted all three of his field-goal kicks and each of his 12 extra-point tries. While the field-goal volume isn't quite there, Detroit's ability to score keeps Bates on the field and scoring. Carolina has allowed a middle-of-the-pack 7.0 points per game to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Bates logged his best game of the season in Week 4 against the Panthers, nailing all four of his field-goal attempts and converting two XPAs. The second-year kicker has now gone a perfect 21-for-21 on boots (seven field goals, 14 extra points) this season. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Bates will look to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Bates has yet to miss a kick this season, nailing eight field-goal attempts and converting all 20 of his XPAs across five games. While the field-goal usage hasn't quite been there, the touchdown-scoring ability of Detroit's offense has kept Bates on the field. He'll face a Green Bay squad that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (4.2) to kickers this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: C.J. Stroud has turned the ball over nine times in Houston's last three games, dating back to the start of last season's playoffs. He'll face a Bengals defense in Week 2 that just forced three turnovers from Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two TDs in Week 1 against the Bills but fumbled away Houston's chance to win the game in the final minute. The Texans' vaunted defense faces another tough test against Joe Burrow and the Bengals, so Stroud and the offense will be relied upon to keep pace. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in superflex or two-QB formats but ranks outside the starting range in single-QB leagues.
outlooksByWeek.3: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.
outlooksByWeek.4: C.J. Stroud has missed top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) over Houston's past two games, failing to throw a touchdown pass in Week 2 and producing just 167 passing yards in Week 3. The Texans fell to 0-3 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. On the bright side, the Texans rebounded from an 0-3 start last season to finish 12-5, and Collins has a realistic chance to return versus Dallas. If Stroud gets his top target back, the slumping QB would have a nice opportunity to get on track as a strong superflex or second fantasy QB against a weak Cowboys secondary that has allowed a 7:0 TD:INT through three games in 2026 after giving up the most QB production in the league last season. Should Collins sit again, Stroud would be a risky choice in all formats despite the favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.5: C.J. Stroud has some streaming appeal in single-QB formats for Week 5, when the Texans travel to Tennessee for a battle between 0-4 AFC South squads. He has thrown for at least 347 yards in two of Houston's four losses and has a 5:0 TD:INT. The Titans have been respectable against the pass, with only four touchdowns allowed through the air this season, but other teams were able to build leads and run effectively on Tennessee. The Texans are unlikely to find as much success on the ground, considering RBs David Montgomery and Woody Marks have combined to average 2.9 yards per carry this season. Stroud has been asked to throw the ball 38 times per game, and he's likely to remain busy in Week 5. The Texans got top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence in Week 4, and Collins contributed immediately in his return by catching both of Stroud's touchdown passes in a 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
outlooksByWeek.6: C.J. Stroud could have a key new target for Houston's pivotal Week 6 clash with the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London. The Texans are just 1-4 and have already fallen three games behind Jacksonville in the standings, but Stroud is quietly averaging a career-high 280 passing yards per game to go with a 6:0 TD:INT. Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and second-most passing yards per game, so Stroud will likely be asked to carry Houston's offense again in Week 6, making him a viable starting QB in fantasy. The Texans notched their first win of the season in Week 5 over the Titans and promptly traded for disgruntled Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison, who hasn't lived up to the hype as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft but excelled at Ohio State while catching passes from Stroud in 2022. Harrison likely won't be fully up to speed, but he could still provide an upgrade over Houston's current wideouts behind Nico Collins.
outlooksByWeek.7: C.J. Stroud is averaging a career-high 286 passing yards per game and has posted a 9:1 TD:INT heading into Houston's Week 7 home game against the Giants. He threw a season-high three touchdown passes in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville while topping 300 yards for the third time in six starts. The Giants have surrendered 12 passing TDs, which is sixth-most in the NFL, and their three rushing scores allowed to QBs are tied for the most in the league, though they have also notched six interceptions. Stroud has consistently been asked to put the Texans' offense on his back due to the team's weak running game, and he has mostly been up to the challenge, so he remains a fringe fantasy starter for Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Johnson paced New Orleans' tight ends in yards (53) during the Week 1 overtime loss but trailed Noah Fant in receptions (three to four) and targets (seven to eight). Despite this, Johnson was on the field for 72 of the Saints' 90 offensive snaps, where Fant played just 37. Thus, Johnson is expected to remain New Orleans' top TE option against a Ravens defense that allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points to the position in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1, Johnson paced the Saints' tight end corps in receptions, targets and yards in Week 2. He ranks third on the team in targets and yards, which is a positive outlook for his value going forward. However, Johnson is in for an unfavorable matchup, as Las Vegas' defense has allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top weapons in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has been New Orleans' second-most productive receiver this season, catching 15 of 19 targets for 173 yards and three touchdowns. With head coach Kellen Moore's offense throwing the ball an average of 44 times per game through three weeks, Johnson is expected to remain one of fantasy's top tight ends going forward. Additionally, he's in for a terrific Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed 17.2 PPR fantasy points per game to the TE position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Johnson had another productive outing in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, catching six of eight targets for 59 yards. He's now tallied 232 receiving yards through four contests this season, the fourth-most amongst tight ends. Johnson will likely continue to benefit from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense that's averaged 45 pass attempts per game this year. Despite this, Johnson is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Johnson tallied just 16 yards on four receptions in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, struggling alongside the rest of New Orleans' offense. Despite this, he's tied for the second-most receptions (25) on the Saints through five weeks, accumulating 248 yards and three touchdowns. Expect Johnson to bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's allowed 14.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Juwan Johnson will look to bounce back from a lackluster performance in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Johnson has struggled over the last two weeks, catching just four of seven targets for 16 yards. Despite this, he remains third on the team in targets (35), receptions (25) and yards (248) through six games, suggesting more fantasy production in the near future. Johnson is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, however, as Pittsburgh's defense has allowed just 11.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keon Coleman doesn't appear to have a meaningful role in the Bills' offense entering Week 2 against the Lions. Despite playing 52% of the team's offensive snaps, Coleman drew only one target, which resulted in a one-yard catch. Always a candidate for an end-zone jump ball, Coleman is no better than fourth in the target pecking order, suggesting he's unlikely to contribute despite an inviting matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keon Coleman will look to build on a mild breakout when the Bills face the Chargers in Week 3. He hauled in six passes last week, his highest total since Week 1 of 2025, as the Bills lost DJ Moore (shoulder) early in Week 2. The Chargers have been more vulnerable to slot options than bigger outside receivers, and Moore's availability remains in flux. With the Bills offense clicking at all levels, Coleman can still garner enough volume to be a deep-league flex consideration.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Patriots. Dealing with a Week 3 ankle injury, Coleman caught a 37-yard pass on two targets, a significant decrease in volume with DJ Moore healthy. Moore dominates targets and Buffalo is a run-first offense. Facing a defense that's allowing a mere 6.6 yards per target, there may not be enough opportunities for Coleman to contribute.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains unsettled ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. DJ Moore exited Week 4 after aggravating a shoulder injury that forced a similar result in Week 2, and Coleman again shined. In the two games with Moore leaving early, Coleman has 12 catches on 13 targets for 179 yards and a touchdown. With Moore playing four quarters, Coleman has two catches for 38 yards. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards leaves Coleman as a fantasy risk regardless of Moore's status.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keon Coleman brings inconsistent volume in the Bills' passing game into a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Coleman saw just two targets in Week 5 despite the absence of DJ Moore, marking the third time in five outings he's drawn that limited amount of volume. Buffalo remains a run-first offense and while Coleman has shown red zone and downfield ability, the lack of consistent volume leads to volatility against a Las Vegas secondary that's allowing the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts, though has been more vulnerable over the middle of late than to boundary receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: So far, so bust for Coleman, who has struggled to make an impact after being selected 33rd overall in the 2024 draft. After flashing in a situational deep-threat role as a rookie (15.0 aDOT), Coleman saw more high percentage looks in 2025 (11.2 aDOT). That led to a much better catch rate (from 51% to 66%), but a big dip in yardage (19.2 YPR to 10.9). Coleman has yet to emerge as a reliable, full-time starter and was even a healthy scratch at times last season. Perhaps the 23-year-old will make a Year 3 leap with Joe Brady now running the show, but he'll have his hands full overtaking DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir atop the depth chart. Coleman is only worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for those matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.
