outlooksByWeek.4: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matt Gay continues to benefit from the Raiders' surprisingly strong start to the season on offense with Kirk Cousins under center. In a Week 4 loss to Kansas City, Gay was a perfect 4-for-4 on FG tries while also converting his only PAT. The veteran has yet to miss an attempt in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 9-for-9 on extra points, putting him third in the NFL in kicker scoring behind the Vikings' Will Reichard and the Colts' Spencer Shrader. Gay likely won't be able to afford to start squandering opportunities in Week 5 against a Patriots team that's allowed 19.3 points per game so far, tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matt Gay missed his first kick of the season in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, pinging the upright on a field goal attempt from 48 yards out. He's still having a strong season, converting all 11 of his PATs and going 11-for-12 on FG attempts, including his only attempt from 50-plus yards. Gay has benefited from a surprisingly potent offense under Kirk Cousins, but the veteran QB may be reverting to his usual level, perhaps opening the door for first overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take the reins, so it's not necessarily bad news for Gay's long-term outlook. Gay will take on a Bills team in Week 6 that's allowing 28.2 points per game, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matt Gay stayed busy in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, going a perfect 3-for-3 on both field goal attempts and extra points. The veteran kicker has benefited from the team's offensive resurgence under new head coach Klint Kubiak, and Gay sits third in scoring in the NFL behind the Colts' Spencer Shrader and the Bills' Tyler Bass. Gay will face a Rams team in Week 7 that's allowed 23.0 points per game, tied for 17th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will likely have Drew Lock throwing balls to him when Seattle faces Arizona in Week 2. Lock took over for an injured Sam Darnold (glute) in the Seahawks' season-opening win, and Darnold is expected to miss Week 2. However, the QB change didn't impact Smith-Njigba's stat line in Week 1, as he finished with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown. He's as matchup-proof a WR as there is in the NFL, and he's set to take on a Cardinals defense that allowed Ladd McConkey (ribs) to put up a 5-82-1 line in less than a full game during a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off another huge game as Seattle prepares to host the Chargers in Week 4. Versus Washington in Week 3, Smith-Njigba recorded 10 catches on 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The star receiver has logged at least eight catches, 120 yards and one score in each of his first three games this season, making him among fantasy's most valuable assets once again. The Chargers don't figure to be able to contain Smith-Njigba given that they're allowing 9.76 yards per target to wideouts, fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaxon Smith-Njigba should once again be the centerpiece of Seattle's passing game in a big Week 5 clash against the 49ers. The star wideout posted a fine 5-76-0 receiving line against the Chargers this past Sunday, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. It's telling that despite his final stats being quite adequate, Smith-Njigba's targets, catches and yards were each a season-low mark in what has been a standout campaign thus far. San Francisco is allowing just 6.96 yards per target to wideouts though four weeks (fifth-best in the league), though Smith-Njigba has proven to be essentially matchup-proof since the beginning of last season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is arguably the most matchup-proof wideout in the NFL, but he could be challenged in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Smith-Njigba caught five of eight targets for 102 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco in a loss this past Sunday. He's now recorded at least 100 receiving yards and one touchdown in four of his five games this season, and Smith-Njigba leads the league with 583 receiving yards. He'll be matched up Week 6 against a Broncos defense that has allowed the third-lowest catch rate (54.5%) to wideouts, but Smith-Njigba figures to get a big boost by not having to face star cornerback Patrick Surtain, who is expected to miss the contest due to an ankle injury.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks return home for a Week 7 interconference clash against the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. He corralled 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6, setting season highs in receptions and targets. Smith-Njigba paced his team in all receiving categories despite a quiet first half, and he now owns a 49-717-7 line on 65 targets through six outings. Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs will try to make it tough on the 2025 Offensive Player of the Year.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games. The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4. He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase Brown and the Bengals are on the road for a divisional clash against the Ravens in Week 7. He registered 13 carries for 39 yards and caught three of four targets for 21 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Brown took a backseat to Samaje Perine, who had 14 carries for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown. Over his last two outings, he's rushed 22 times for 49 yards, a miserable 2.2 yards per carry. Next up is another difficult matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 18.6 fantasy points per game (7th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. McMillan is coming off the best performance of his young career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, recording career highs in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (192) while scoring two touchdowns. He ranks ninth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.3) through four appearances this season, leading Carolina in yards, targets and receptions. Expect McMillan to remain productive in Week 6 against an Eagles secondary that's allowed 38.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of Carolina's top wideouts in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan has been one of the league's most productive wideouts this season, catching 32 of 48 targets for 471 yards and two touchdowns in just five contests. He's averaged 94.2 receiving yards per game, the seventh-best mark in the NFL, and is expected to continue benefitting from the Panthers' aggressive style of offense (40.2 pass attempts per game). Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers secondary that's allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming those duties is an open question for Denver. Waddle will try to hit paydirt again in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle in his first season with the Broncos. He's been held to 35 receiving yards or fewer in four of five games, including a 2-19-0 line on five targets in a Week 5 win over the Chargers. Having Sean Payton reclaim play-calling duties should help the offense in the long run, but Waddle will be tough to trust until he begins to display consistent chemistry with Bo Nix. Waddle will face a Seahawks secondary in Week 6 that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Waddle remains stuck in neutral as part of a sluggish Broncos passing game. The former Dolphin has gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards, managing just a 13-88-1 line on 25 targets over that stretch while quarterback Bo Nix tries to find a rhythm. Waddle showed his upside back in Week 2 with an 8-138-0 line, but until the Denver offense begins clicking, his production will remain erratic. He could break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers this season, 31st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.
outlooksByWeek.5: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: D'Andre Swift could be in line for a featured role once again as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Swift should have benefited hugely from Kyle Monangai being out with a toe injury in Week 5, but he rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 30 yards in a blowout loss. The status of Monangai remains up in the air ahead of Chicago's away bout, and Swift's value is very much contingent on his position mate's status. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: D'Andre Swift could see his workload take a hit as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Swift was inefficient on the ground in Week 6 with 16 carries for 44 yards, but he was able to salvage his outing with two rushing touchdowns and four catches for 26 yards. The veteran has benefited from Kyle Monangai being out the last two weeks with turf toe, especially given that three of his six touchdowns this season have come in that stretch. Whether Monangai plays or not, Swift will face a New England front that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Williams will aim to build on a stellar return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Williams had no struggles in Week 6 against the Falcons in his first game since Week 2, completing 83 percent of passes for 305 yards and one touchdown. The third-year quarterback has now surpassed 250 passing yards in both games that he's played through this season, and the sky's the limit now. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brandon Aubrey was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. With New York dominating time of possession, Aubrey did not even attempt a field goal. He also missed one of his extra points when Javonte Williams was assessed a taunting penalty following a touchdown, leading to a 48-yard PAT try. Aubrey has nowhere to go but up in Week 2 versus the Commanders, though. Washington allowed 26.5 points per game just a season ago, which was 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three of his field goals last game for Dallas, including a 60-yarder. Aubrey also booted four extra points, shaking off a surprising miss in Week 1 versus the Giants. In Week 3, the Cowboys clash with the Ravens. Baltimore is allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is in the middle of the pack so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and two extra points last game for Dallas, but his missed three-pointer will likely be the most talked about boot. Aubrey was blocked from 59 yards out, a makeable distance for the strong-legged kicker, and the Cowboys lost to the Ravens by that margin. However, Aubrey has made six field goals in the last two games, and remains a standout option kicking for one of the top offenses in the league. In Week 4, Dallas will face a disappointing Houston squad allowing 25 points per contest, which is 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brandon Aubrey missed two field goals last game for Dallas. Such a sensational headline needs explanation, though, as both of Aubrey's misses came from over 60 yards away. Aubrey had a 62-yarder blocked, and missed a 65-yarder wide left. Otherwise, Aubrey connected on two field goals from 50 yards and in, while also making all four of his extra points. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay squad allowing 24.0 points per clash, which is tied for 19th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brandon Aubrey did not have much work last game for Dallas. Aubrey connected on one field goal and one extra point in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Aubrey has made just nine field goals through five games for Dallas, which is tied for 10th in the league. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers. Green Bay is allowing 22.4 points per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brandon Aubrey managed one single, solitary extra point last game for Dallas. The Cowboys offense has sputtered of late, scoring a combined 29 points over the last two contests. Aubrey has registered just one field goal and two PATs over that span. In Week 7, Dallas will look to right the ship against another struggling NFC East squad, the Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per tilt, which is 16th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Likely has remained extremely busy for the Giants, regardless of who lines up at quarterback. Likely has received double-digit targets in four of the last five games for the G-Men. Likely has scored three times in the last two contests, and five times on the season overall. Likely leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and touchdowns, and is second in receptions to Trey McBride. Likely should be primed for another big outing in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jared Goff will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Goff recorded another monster performance heading into Detroit's bye week, and he's yet to throw an interception this season. The veteran quarterback has now completed 67 percent of passes for 1,485 yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions in five games. He'll face a Green Bay defense that allowed 258 passing yards and a 1:2 TD:INT ratio to Dak Prescott in Week 6.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Gunnar Helm finished third on the Titans with 28 receiving yards on six targets in the season-opening loss to the Jets. He's locked in as Tennessee's top TE heading into Week 2 against the Eagles, but Helm isn't a recommended fantasy option outside of super-deep fantasy formats given the struggles of the Titans' entire offense. Helm has recorded at least four catches in five of his last eight games, but the 2025 fourth-round pick has just two games with more than 36 receiving yards in his career and two TDs in 17 NFL appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Gunnar Helm is tied for second on the Titans with seven targets through two games, but he has just 41 receiving yards. The 2025 fourth-round pick is locked in as the team's starting TE heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, who just allowed six catches for 54 yards and a TD to Rams TE Terrance Ferguson. Helm is unlikely to match that production considering he has yet to exceed 51 receiving yards in a game while scoring just twice through 18 NFL appearances. Unless second-year Titans QB Cam Ward starts to pick up his passing production, Helm can continue to be ignored in the vast majority of fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.4: Gunnar Helm is third on the Titans through three weeks with eight catches and 11 targets, but the 2025 fourth-round pick has mustered a meager 55 receiving yards. His fantasy appeal is minimal for Week 4 against the Ravens, even though Baltimore's defense has allowed a TD to a TE in two of three games this season. Helm has reached 40 receiving yards in just two of 19 NFL appearances.
outlooksByWeek.5: Gunnar Helm is averaging just 15 receiving yards per game heading into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans. The second-year TE has exceeded 70% of offensive snaps in every game this season, but Helm is being used more as a blocker than a pass catcher in Tennessee's struggling offense. Houston is allowing 56 yards per game to TEs but hasn't given up a TD to the position, while Helm has scored just twice in 20 career NFL games. Helm hasn't done enough to warrant fantasy consideration.
outlooksByWeek.6: Gunnar Helm remains a fantasy non-factor heading into Week 6 against the Colts, as Tennessee's starting TE is averaging just 12 receiving yards per game. Helm has played over 70% of offensive snaps in every game this season, but he's used primarily as a blocker. The Colts are tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to TEs with four, but Helm has scored only twice through 21 career NFL appearances.
outlooksByWeek.7: Gunnar Helm has been trending in the wrong direction, with consecutive zero-catch performances coming into a Week 7 home game against the Browns and just nine catches for 60 yards all season. He continues to lead Tennessee's TEs in playing time, but Helm has been used almost exclusively as a blocker in recent weeks. Helm remains a non-factor for fantasy purposes in Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Helm quietly caught 44 passes during his rookie season, which -- believe it or not -- ranks 11th among rookie tight ends over the past decade. Impressively, the 2025 fourth-round pick hit that mark despite playing second fiddle to starter Chig Okonkwo. Helm, who caught a healthy 79% of his 56 targets, wasn't much of a fantasy option as a rookie (5.7 PPG), but with Okonkwo out of the picture, he's positioned for a much larger role in his second season. Helm will need a leap from QB Cam Ward, but if that happens, a breakout season is possible. The 24-year-old is worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaac TeSlaa remains a touchdown-dependent option as the Lions take on the Bills in Week 2. TeSlaa was unable to convert on his one target in Week 1 against the Saints, which only made season hopes lower for him after a subpar training camp. He also remains the fifth option in the Detroit passing game behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta. Luckily, Buffalo gave up a whopping 40.0 PPR points to Houston wide receivers in Week 1, so this upcoming week could be TeSlaa's chance to return to relevance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. TeSlaa recorded his first catches of the season against the Bills in Week 2, reeling in two of five targets for 26 yards. While his final stat line was still modest, the second-year receiver's five targets are promising. With that being said, he still hasn't done enough to be considered more than a depth option, especially against a New York defense that's been tougher on wide receivers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaac TeSlaa will look to replicate a solid performance as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. TeSlaa started the season quietly with just two catches for 26 yards across the first two games, but he reeled in all three targets for 66 yards against the Jets in Week 3. While this output isn't enough to warrant a start and is more translatable to a stash move, TeSlaa could be in store for more looks. The Panthers have also allowed a second-least 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaac TeSlaa could continue to have a big role as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. TeSlaa finished Week 4 against the Panthers with season-high targets, catches and yards, reeling in four of eight looks for four catches and 95 yards. After a slow start to the season, the second-year pass catcher has now posted a 7-161-0 receiving line in the last two games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to the wide receiver position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaac TeSlaa will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. After it appeared the second-year pass catcher was starting to carve out a role for himself again, TeSlaa recorded zero catches against the Cardinals before Detroit's bye. Hopefully the second game this year with zero catches was another anomaly, as there is plenty of love to spread with the Lions' high-volume offense. Green Bay has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: TeSlaa is a candidate for a Year 2 leap as the favorite for No. 3 WR duties in Detroit behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. TeSlaa barely played as a rookie (27 total targets), but he had a very specific role and, believe it or not, tied for 11th in the entire NFL with 11 end zone targets. That helped lead to six touchdowns, four of which came when his snaps increased during Detroit's final six games. The 2025 third-round pick has a big size edge on both St. Brown and Williams, so while consistent targets are a long shot, he's still likely to remain busy near the goal line. TeSlaa won't be more than a boom/bust situational target most weeks, but if one of the starters misses time, he'll be on the flex radar. Consider him with a late pick.

outlooksByWeek.3: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big performance when Seattle faces Washington in Week 3. With Jadarian Price suffering a shoulder injury against Arizona on Sunday, Wilson stepped up and led the Seahawks with 21 rushes for 92 yards. Price's injury isn't considered serious, but it's not certain that he'll be able to return to action in Week 3. Whoever leads Seattle's backfield will be looking to score the first rushing touchdown against the Commanders this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emanuel Wilson may be moving into a timeshare at running back for Seattle heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. An early fumble by rookie Jadarian Price was partly responsible for Wilson leading the Seahawks with nine carries in a Week 3 win over Washington, with Price logging just five totes and George Holani three. With that said, Wilson managed a paltry 14 yards on his carries, so he didn't exactly make a loud statement in a bid for more work. The Chargers just gave up 154 rushing yards to Buffalo's James Cook in Week 3, so they could be vulnerable on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big Week 4 performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Wilson led his team's backfield this past Sunday against the Chargers, posting a 21-81-1 line on the ground. Equally promising was his 3-39-1 line as a pass catcher after he logged zero receptions over the first three weeks of the campaign. With Jadarian Price (chest) on IR, Wilson figures to continue to work as Seattle's No. 1 RB, though the eventual return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) could shake up the backfield. Charbonnet isn't expected to be ready for Week 5, however, so Wilson will likely get plenty of work against the 49ers, who are middle-of-the-pack so far in giving up 17.4 fantasy points per game to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emanuel Wilson will look to get into the end zone for a third straight game when the Seahawks travel to Denver in Week 6. Wilson has emerged as Seattle's clear top RB over the past two weeks, registering 41 carries for 142 yards and two touchdowns on the ground along with five catches for 50 yards and another score through the air in that span. He figures to continue working as the team's No. 1 RB at least until one or both of Zach Charbonnet (knee) or Jadarian Price (chest) is able to return, but that won't happen in Week 6. The Broncos have been vulnerable against the run this season, surrendering 4.51 yards per carry to running backs (eighth-worst in the league).
outlooksByWeek.7: Emanuel Wilson and the Seahawks play host to the Chiefs for a Week 7 clash on Sunday Night Football. He had 14 carries for 52 yards and failed to catch his only target during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. It was an underwhelming performance for Wilson, who had scored three touchdowns over his previous two outings. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) practicing and likely to make his 2026 season debut in Week 7, it's probably best to avoid the Seahawks backfield versus Kansas City's defense that's tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyrone Tracy was the third-string running back in the season opener for the Giants while Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1, though that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly. Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Tracy does suit up in Week 2, he will act mostly as depth against a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyrone Tracy was the most productive back last game for the Giants, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown. However, he managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches overall. Meanwhile, Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches, Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries and Cam Skattebo did not even register a touch following last week's costly fumble. It will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. In Week 7, the Giants will also face a stingy Texans run defense. Houston is allowing only 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Tracy is set to compete with Devin Singletary for opportunities in a Giants backfield led by second-year back Cam Skattebo. Tracy has produced 200-plus touches and 1,000-plus yards in each of his first two NFL seasons, but that doesn't tell the full story. Tracy got there as a fifth-round rookie in 2024 by impressing and taking New York's starting gig by Week 5. Last season, he quickly lost lead-back duties to Skattebo, but played a much larger role once Skattebo went down for the season with an injury (9.0 touches per game during Weeks 1-9, but 18.6 per game from Weeks 10-18). Tracy has no standalone fantasy value, but he's effective as a rusher and receiver. That makes the 26-year-old a solid backup who would be worth adding if Skattebo misses additional time.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

outlooksByWeek.2: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 battle with the Patriots. The rookie should remain on waiver wires after playing just three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps in their season-opening win. Bernard is below DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, and Pat Freiermuth on the food chain, and it would take an absence or two from his teammates for him to see an uptick in playing time.
outlooksByWeek.3: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Germie Bernard and the Steelers travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He caught his only target for 14 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 victory in Week 3. One week after leading the team in yardage while finishing second in targets, Bernard fell victim to a Steelers offense that prefers to spread the ball around, as Aaron Rodgers completed passes to nine different receivers in the win. Cleveland's defense is susceptible through the air, as they're tied for 29th in receiving TDs allowed (5) through three games, but Bernard is off the fantasy radar for now.
outlooksByWeek.5: Germie Bernard and the Steelers return home to square off against the Colts in Week 5. The rookie wideout caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. Bernard should remain on fantasy benches while playing behind veterans DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, and Jaylen Warren, along with tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington. Indianapolis allows 35.0 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 20th, but his limited involvement on offense doesn't inspire much confidence.
outlooksByWeek.6: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He hauled in six of nine targets for 80 yards and had one carry for four yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 Week 5 victory. With Roman Wilson (finger) injured in the win and already ruled out for the meeting with the Buccaneers, Bernard has a real opportunity to fill that void and continue contributing in his debut season. The 2026 second-round pick notched career highs but is still searching for his first career touchdown, something he hopes to change against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Paris for an interconference clash against the Saints in Week 7. He caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and the game-winning touchdown in Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime win in Week 6. The rookie erupted for career highs in every receiving category while notching his first-ever TD. Bernard tied DK Metcalf (11-93-0) for the team lead in receptions while finishing a close second in yardage and targets. He'll aim to stay hot against a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th by allowing 32.3 fantasy points per game to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third or fourth in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr., DK Metcalf and perhaps Roman Wilson. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so he's only worth draft consideration in the later rounds.
